steps.text: Dissolve yeast and sugar in warm water in a large bowl. Let sit until creamy, about 10 minutes.

Stir whole wheat flour, oil, and salt into yeast mixture, then stir in 4 cups bread flour. Add remaining 1 1/2 cups bread flour, 1/2 cup at a time, stirring well after each addition. When dough pulls together, turn it out onto a lightly floured surface and knead until smooth and elastic, about 8 minutes.
Lightly oil a large mixing bowl. Place dough into the bowl and turn to coat with oil. Cover with a damp cloth and let rise in a warm place until doubled in size, about 1 hour.
Punch down dough and turn it out onto a lightly floured surface. Divide into thirds and form each piece into a round. Cover and let rest for 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Stephen's Pizza Dough
raw_recipe.description: This recipe uses both bread flour and whole-wheat flour to make three flavorful pizza crusts, which means you can freeze some for later use.

review.reviewBody: I have not made this recipe yet, but while reading the reviews I noticed many people having trouble ending up with a soggy crust and overcooked toppings. To avoid this, you must work with a pizza stone and a pizza peel. Place the stone in your oven, preheat the oven to 500 degrees. Allow the pizza stone to heat for 30 minutes at this temperature. Meanwhile prepare your pizza on your floured pizza peel (be sure to give your pizza crust a little shake on the peel prior to putting on your toppings so that you can add more flour if necessary - doing this will ensure that it will slide off easily onto the stone ). Once you are sure your pizza will slide off easily, top it however you want and then slide it very carefully onto the stone in the oven. Heating the stone for 30 minutes prior to baking the pizza will ensure a thoroughly cooked crispy pizza crust. Watch your pizza very carefully as it will cook fast at this temperature.

Excellent recipe. Have made this many, many times. I change up the flour sometimes to try different brands and variations. Will swap corn oil for olive oil occasionally. Pre-heat pizza stone on the grill to around 600 degrees. Thin crusts will cook in about 4-5 minutes. Just like a regular pizza joint!!

I use this recipe all the time. Add oregano and garlic to dough. Freezes very well - just lightly oil and wrap a couple times in Saran. Remove from freezer about 3-4 hours before needed. Cook at 500F using a pizza stone. Enjoy!!

I made this pizza dough completely last minute for an impromptu dinner party of about four families with kids. I made all three pizzas and nothing was left, it was a huge hit! I didn’t want to wait for my dough to rise for an hour so I cheated by putting it in an oiled Dutch oven and covered with a well dampened kitchen towel and then stuck it in my oven on warm for about fifteen to twenty minutes. Worked perfectly as a short cut! One thing; my husband’s family is in the pizza business and so I followed their lead and poked the uncooked crust with a fork all over several times and then brushed really lightly with olive oil. It cooked nice and evenly with no over crisp or raw spots to speak of. Definitely using this recipe again!

This recipe is spot on! Be sure to not overwork your dough (per the norm with any dough), or it can turn out a bit tougher than desired. Preheat your pizza stone for about 10-15 mins at 350 and use a pizza peal with either flour or yellow corn meal to get it to slide off easily. Pre-bake crust on stone for approx 10mins at 350 and then while you are adding your favorite toppings, allow the oven to heat up to 425 for your final cook of the pizza for about 10-15 minutes. And there you have it! Amazing, fresh, all your own, tasty pizza! ENJOY!

This pizza dough was very good. It’s one of the first recipes I’ve made from Allrecipes that I didn’t change any ingredients.We divided it into 2 crusts because we like a thicker crust. Precooked the rolled out crust at 375* for 10 minutes, cooked with the toppings on the pan for about 10 minutes and then slid the pizza off to the rack for about 8 minutes.Very good pizza! We will make many more times.

I'll preface with the fact that I have made homemade dough maybe twice in my life, never pizza dough. I followed the recipe for the dough. But after I separated it into 3 bowls, I left it on the counter for about two hours - covered with seran wrap. It more than doubled in size (again). I thought I'd have enough dough to make 6 pizzas and planned to freeze half. But it deflated again when I touched it. So we made 3. I did things differently than the recipe suggests at this point. I didn't use a rolling pin, but pulled it apart with my hands. Then I laid the dough on a parchment paper lined cookie sheet that was sprinkled with corn meal. I pre-baked the crusts for 7 minutes at 400* (I should have prebaked for 10 as one crust was doughy in the center). Once out of the oven, and cooled a bit, I brushed the crust with olive oil then sprinkled on parm. cheese, garlic salt and italian seasoning. Next time I'll be relatively liberal with the garlic salt. My kids all decorated half a pizza with their favorite sauces & toppings. Then we baked them for an addition 12-15 minutes at 450*. They were a hit! One crust recipe made probably what dominos would call 3 medium pizzas. The crusts were not thin, but much like dominos hand-tossed or digiorno rising crust. They fed 2 adults and 3 preschool aged children with 1/2 of a pizza left over. I attached a photo.

I made this pizza but made a few changes. I used all purpose flour 5•1/2 cups. I did not add the 1/2 cup of wheat flour. And , I made two pizza's out of the dough not three. It came out excellent. Thick and moist. Best pizza ever!

With a few changes this recipe works. I skipped the whole wheat flour, used a full 7 cups of all-purpose flour (I didn't have any bread flour on hand) and added about a half tablespoon garlic powder. When kneading the dough, I had to add quite a bit of flour as it was VERY sticky. Be generous with the oil during the rising process, which took about 2 hours to double. I used for calzones & it worked just fine.

I used this recipe for a school project, and everyone loved it! Instead of adding four cups and then the rest, I added the flour by slowly folding it in (1/2 cup at a time) until it reached the consistency I preferred. 

Then instead of adding the toppings and immediately cooking it, I shaped the dough on a pizza stone and cooked until the crust started to brown. I then added the sauce and cheese (and other toppings), then put it back in the oven until the cheese had melted. This prevents the dough from getting soggy, as it cooks the bottom of the pizza before adding the liquid of the sauces. 

Also optional: add olive oil to the crust after adding the cheese and toppings to give the crust a more golden brown color.

I made this recipe for my kids sleepover party. All the kids got to make their own mini pizzas and they loved it. I cut the recipe into three as described and then cut each of the 3 sections into thirds. Rolled them thin and everyone topped as they liked. Crust was great. I did make some adjustments to deal with what I had on hand. Instead of whole wheat flour I used gluten free flour, did 2 tsp regular salt and 2 tsp garlic salt and used 2 tsp of italian seasoning.
It came out SOOOO well!! I do recommend cooking it for a bit longer than recommended though! Our pizza was still very doughy
I find the recipe a it bland. I also had to add much more flour than it called for. The dough was never pulling away from my stand mixer.
So easy to do .my family favorite
It's easy to make and has good stretch for calzone.
I've made this several times. Outstanding pizza crust! Rises well around the edges. Like free bread sticks! If you preheat your pizza stone you get a nice crisp bottom.

Good dough. Followed the directions and it turned out really good. I can only cook 1 pizza at a time in my oven. I should have waited and kneaded the dough again before baking the second pizza. It rose more than I wanted after I put the toppings on.
